info.title: Inji Interoperability Playground API
info.description: Runs verifiable credential flows issuer -> wallet -> verifier across Inji modules and independent reference implementations, records every HTTP exchange, and reports pass/fail per combination.

get.summary: Registered roles with their capabilities and current health
get.description: One entry per implementation that can play the issuer, wallet or verifier role: its descriptor (formats, proof types, DID methods, protocol profiles, version) and the result of a health probe (cached for 5 s).

get.summary: Health and image tags of the local Inji stack, plus the health of every role
Scenarios a run can apply: the happy path and the tamper variants, with expected outcomes
Whether one issuer x wallet x verifier x format combination can run, and why not
get.description: Compares the three role descriptors. `blocking` reasons make a run end immediately with the verdict `not-supported`; `warning` reasons are shown but the run is attempted.

post.description: Starts one issuer -> wallet -> verifier run in the background and answers with its id; follow it on the WebSocket (`/ws?runId=<id>`) or with `GET /api/runs/{id}`. Send a full configuration, or `replayOf` with the id of a stored run to repeat its configuration (fields sent next to it override the copied ones). A combination the compatibility check rejects is stored at once with the verdict `not-supported`.

get.summary: Run history, newest first, with filters and paging
One run: configuration, status, report once finished, and the action a person must take, if any
Events of a run in the order they were emitted (the messages the WebSocket streams)

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events after this sequence number

get.summary: HTTP exchanges recorded during a run, in order, with full headers and bodies

post.summary: Cancel a queued or running run
post.description: The run stops at once; its report gets the verdict `error` with the code `run.cancelled`.

post.summary: Confirm that the person did what the run is waiting for (manual fallback)
post.description: Used when the server cannot observe the person's action itself, for example a wallet app on a phone whose traffic does not pass through the playground.

post.summary: Deliver a signal from a verifier component running outside the server
post.description: The Inji Verify React SDK runs in the browser and reports through callbacks; the UI forwards `onVPReceived(transactionId)` (kind `vp-received`), `onVPProcessed` and `onError` here, and the run's verifier role receives them in order through `RunContext.waitForCallback()`.

get.summary: Interoperability report of a finished run, as JSON
get.description: The stored report (issuer, wallet, verifier, format, proof type, outcome, verdict, error) plus the versions of every component, each step with its label and duration, the failing exchange with links into the inspector, and the credential size. 409 while the run is still going.

get.summary: Interoperability report of a finished run, as Markdown
get.description: The same content as `report.json`, rendered as a Markdown document whose first table holds the problem statement fields: issuer, wallet, verifier, format, proof type, outcome and error detail.

get.summary: Everything stored about a run, with secrets redacted
get.description: Run, events, exchanges and artefacts in one document, safe to attach to an issue. Access, refresh and ID tokens, authorization and pre-authorized codes, transaction codes, client secrets, cookies, authorization headers and private JWK members are replaced by `[redacted sha256:<8 hex>]`; credentials, presentations and verification results are kept because they are the evidence. Works for runs that are still going.

get.summary: Compatibility matrix: newest run per cell, plus cells that cannot run and why
get.description: A cell is issuer x wallet x verifier x format x OpenID4VP profile x scenario. Cells with a stored run show the verdict of the newest finished one and the counts of all of them; every other combination of registered roles (for the `scenario` given, `happy` by default) is listed from the compatibility check as `untested` or `not-supported` with the blocking reasons. `format=md` answers with a dated Markdown document instead of JSON.

get.summary: Success rate and p50/p95 durations per step, role pair and flow; credential sizes
get.description: Computed from the finished runs that match the filters. Success rate of a step: ok / ran; of a role pair: phases whose steps all finished ok / phases attempted (issuance = issuer -> wallet, presentation = wallet -> verifier); of a flow and overall: pass / (pass + fail + error). Percentiles use the nearest-rank method. Credential sizes give bytes and the PixelPass QR text length with a fits-a-version-40-QR flag.

get.summary: The same metrics in the Prometheus text format
Interoperability gaps found so far, from docs/gaps/gaps.json
get.description: Entries of the gap register with the matrix cells they explain. Security-relevant entries (`disclosure: private`) are reduced to id, repository and severity. An absent register gives `source: null` and no gaps; entries that do not match the schema are listed under `problems`.
